CHIEF COMPLAINT
Referral from emergency room for evaluation of chest pain and possible esophagitis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 58-year-old female, new patient, who presented to the emergency room approximately 3 months ago in early October with acute onset chest pain. Pain was sudden in onset, did not wake her, and occurred randomly. It was sharp in character, located in the center of the chest behind the breastbone, and felt like she was having a heart attack. Pain was worse with eating. She also experienced associated difficulty swallowing. She tolerated the pain for 4 days before going to the emergency room when nothing relieved her symptoms. The ER performed an EKG and blood tests, which were all normal. The cardiac workup was also normal. The ER team thought the symptoms were related to the GI system and referred her to our clinic. Symptoms resolved approximately 3 days after the ER visit. She has not had any additional episodes of chest pain or swallowing difficulties since that time. Patient recalls being under significant stress from a job transition around the time of symptom onset. She denies current abdominal pain and reports normal bowel movements. She is currently trying to lose weight.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies current chest pain, dysphagia, abdominal pain, or changes in bowel movements. Denies family history of GI problems. No mention of current heartburn but is unsure what heartburn feels like.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Uterine fibroids, anemia, cholecystectomy several years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Not documented.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Denies family history of gastrointestinal problems.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recent job transition causing significant stress, which temporally coincided with her symptoms.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Abdomen: Lower abdomen with no pain or tenderness to palpation. Upper abdominal quadrants with mild tenderness to light palpation bilaterally, unchanged with increased pressure. Otherwise normal examination.

RESULTS
ER EKG: normal. ER blood tests: normal. Cardiac workup: normal.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
58-year-old female with history of acute chest pain and dysphagia 3 months ago that has completely resolved. Differential diagnosis includes GERD, dyspepsia, esophagitis, musculoskeletal etiologies, and anxiety. Most likely etiology is an anxiety attack related to job transition with possible musculoskeletal contribution. Discussed EGD (upper endoscopy) versus watchful monitoring. Given that symptoms occurred 3 months ago and have completely resolved, patient is likely asymptomatic and any esophagitis would have healed by now, making EGD unlikely to show pathology. Patient elected to self-monitor for symptoms and will contact the office if she experiences recurrence of pain or other concerning symptoms, at which time EGD can be scheduled. Patient instructed to call office with any additional episodes of pain or symptoms. Follow up as needed for any other GI complaints.
